instruction.text: This is a map of the contiguous United States of America. Select the red rock to learn more.

feedback.end: The contiguous United States of America refers to the 48 states that are all connected together — that’s every state apart from Alaska and Hawaii!

atoms.b: The Grand Canyon is a huge ((++valley house)) in Arizona, that was formed by the Colorado River wearing down rock over 6 million years.
The canyon is mostly ((++red white)), but different layers of rock can be colours such as grey, green, pink and violet.
The canyon is over 6,000 feet deep, and its ((++floor ceiling)) can reach temperatures of up to 50 °C!

instruction.text: Select the Statue of Liberty to learn more.
Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: New York City is the most populated city in the USA with around 8.5 million people.
New York City is also the most visited city in the USA, welcoming over 60 million tourists annually.
New York City’s Statue of Liberty was a gift from France and attracts millions of tourists each year.
New York City’s Wall Street is one of the world’s major centres of finance and banking.

atoms.b: Tornado Alley is an area in the ((++centre west)) of the USA, where tornadoes are 10 times more likely to form.
Here, warm air from near the Equator moves ((++north south)) and meets cooler, dry air. This causes the air to spin and create a twisting funnel.
The deadliest tornado on record was the 2011 Joplin tornado, which ((++caused prevented)) 158 fatalities and over 2 billion dollars in damages.

instruction.text: Select the three animals that can be found in the Everglades.

text.text: The Everglades is a large wetland ecosystem in the south of Florida.

feedback.end: The Everglades is known for its unique wildlife. It is also the only place on Earth where American alligators and crocodiles live together in the wild!

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The Rocky Mountains and Appalachian Mountains are North America’s two major mountain systems, both running through the USA.
atoms.sound: The Rocky Mountains and app-uh-layshn Mountains are North America’s two major mountain systems, both running through the United States.

atoms.text: The Rocky Mountains are situated in the west. They stretch roughly 3,000 miles from the US state of New Mexico all the way to Northwestern Canada. They are known for their rough terrain and extreme weather.

The Appalachians are in the east and span 2,000 miles from Canada to the US state of Alabama. These mountains are more than 250 million years old and almost the entire range is covered in dense forests.
atoms.sound: The app-uh-layshns are in the east, and span 2,000 miles from Canada to the US state of Alabama. These mountains are more than 250 million years old and almost the entire range is covered in dense forests.
